articleSummary: On 2026-03-22, the WHO extended by three months the International Health Regulations (IHR) Emergency Committee designation for the polio situation, maintaining USPII status due to ongoing risks from wild poliovirus and vaccine-derived strains and updating countries requiring mandatory polio vaccination for travelers: Afghanistan, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and the Syrian Arab Republic. The Lake Chad subregion remains at risk for neighboring states—Cameroon, Chad, Niger, and the Central African Republic—where polio vaccination is still advised for travelers. International travel regulations prohibit departure from these five countries without documented polio vaccination; border authorities may block exits. Romanian travelers to these countries who have not been vaccinated in the last 12 months should vaccinate at least four weeks before travel (or immediately in emergencies), with the vaccination recorded on the international certificate.

articleSummary: Thailand: Infective endocarditis caused by dental caries in a 75-year-old Thai man with a history of prior aortic surgery and TEVAR developed bacteremia from dental caries, seeding both the aortic and mitral valves with Streptococcus from oral flora. He presented with fever, fatigue, and progressive dyspnea; imaging showed aortic and mitral valve infections with severe paravalvular leakage. Initial antibiotic therapy improved fever but heart failure symptoms persisted, necessitating urgent surgery: replacement of both valves with porcine tissue valves, redo aortic graft, and vascular reconstructions to maintain cerebral perfusion. Postoperative antibiotics continued for 6 weeks; residual paravalvular leak was subsequently closed via catheter-based approach with clinical improvement and regained exercise tolerance. The report notes dental caries are common in Thailand, and patients with valve disease or prosthetic valves carry lifelong endocarditis risk. It underscores the importance of oral health and antibiotic prophylaxis before dental procedures to prevent bacteremia.

articleSummary: Harbin Institute of Technology surveyed 450 hepatitis B patients in China and identified six major commonalities driving chronic infection. Many carriers are asymptomatic and diagnosed only during routine exams, underscoring the silent nature of hepatitis B. A four-dimensional model is proposed: behavior exposure, immune status, lifestyle rhythm, and protective cognition. The six commonalities are: (1) frequent contact with incompletely sterilized invasive instruments during cosmetic or medical procedures; (2) sharing personal items such as razors, toothbrushes, or nail clippers; (3) long-term immune suppression from lifestyle stress; (4) poor vaccination awareness or failure to recheck anti-HBs antibody titers after vaccination; (5) irregular work–sleep cycles and high-fat, high-sugar diets that burden the liver; (6) cognitive biases about transmission, with underestimation of high-risk exposures and overestimation of safe social contact. Recommendations emphasize using regulated facilities, personal items, timely vaccination with antibody checks, regular liver screening, and health education.

articleSummary: Red urine in cows and buffaloes is a warning sign of several serious diseases, according to Dr. Anil Kumar at Chas Pet Clinic, Bokaro. As of 22 March 2026, the main potential causes include babesiosis (tick fever), bacillary hemoglobinuria, and cystitis (urinary tract infection). Babesiosis, spread by ticks through contact or licking/eating, causes fever, weakness, loss of appetite, and progressive reddened urine. Bacillary hemoglobinuria is a bacterial disease often affecting the liver, leading to red urine and potential fatality if untreated. Cystitis produces pain or discomfort during urination and frequent urination. Common accompanying symptoms include high fever, poor appetite, weakness, and reduced milk yield. Prevention focuses on shedding parasite control: spray the cattle shed with antiparasitic insecticides and regularly treat animals; avoid contaminated fodder; provide nutritious feed. Recovery may take 2–3 days with appropriate treatment, after which normal milk production resumes.

articleSummary: Sporotrichosis caused by Sporothrix brasiliensis, transmitted from cats to humans, is discussed. Most cases occur in Brazil, with some in Uruguay; Spain has reported none. Transmission occurs via scratches or bites from cats, or contact with lesions or wound exudate rich in fungus. In cats, infection causes open sores, crusts, hair loss, and conjunctivitis; in humans, nodules and plaques appear on exposed skin—face, legs, arms—and can ulcerate or form a linear pattern along lymphatic vessels. Mucosal involvement, including the mouth, and eye infections can occur. Early signs include red bumps; severe complications such as meningitis, arthritis, or pneumonia can arise in immunocompromised individuals or those with preexisting health issues. Other feline-to-human diseases include toxoplasmosis (pregnancy risk), Bartonella henselae (scratches/bites), ringworm, and some intestinal parasites. No Spain cases yet.

articleSummary: Sporotrichosis is a subcutaneous fungal infection caused by Sporothrix species, increasingly highlighted in Brazil as a cat-transmitted zoonosis affecting humans and animals in urban areas. Domestic and stray cats harbor high fungal loads in skin lesions and can transmit the infection to people via scratches, bites, or contact with contaminated secretions; transmission between cats occurs chiefly during fights, with dogs less commonly affected. The environment–animal–human transmission pathway, with cats as the main urban vector in Brazil, is central; human-to-human transmission remains unlikely.

A Phu Quoc 11-year-old died from serogroup B meningococcal disease; a classmate was hospitalized in Ho Chi Minh City. In 2025 Vietnam reported 95 meningococcal cases and 3 deaths; southern Vietnam data show serogroup B accounts for 98.1% of cases since 2014–2025, with the highest burden among children under 5 (especially under 1) and youths 15–24. Transmission is via respiratory droplets; incubation is 1–10 days. Illness rapidly evolves to fever, severe headache, vomiting, stiff neck, and purpura; in severe sepsis, adrenal and multi-organ failure can cause death within a day. Survivors often have lifelong disabilities: limb necrosis with amputations, brain injury, seizures, hearing/vision loss, and chronic pain; psychological trauma is common. Vaccination against serogroups B and ACWY is available and recommended for children; hygiene measures and avoiding crowds are advised.

articleSummary: Bemnifosbuvir, a nucleotide/nucleoside analogue, emerges as a promising hepatitis E virus (HEV) inhibitor. articleHeadline: DOH urges Metro Manila residents to undergo TB screening - Manila Standard
articleSummary: Metro Manila (National Capital Region) recorded 101,807 tuberculosis cases in the first 1.5 months of 2026, as of February 16, prompting the Department of Health (DOH) to urge residents to undergo TB screening. Data from the DOH Epidemiology Bureau highlight a surge in detected cases in the region. DOH-MMCHD Regional Director Lester Tan said TB is curable and should not be feared or shamed, stressing that delaying treatment worsens outcomes. The nationwide campaign has already screened more than 3.1 million Filipinos, with the agency pushing for wider implementation of TB Preventive Treatment for high-risk individuals and vulnerable sectors. Public health messages advise watching for symptoms such as a cough lasting more than two weeks, chest pain, fever, and excessive sweating. The initiative emphasizes a united community effort against TB and ongoing prevention efforts in Metro Manila.

articleSummary: Suriname’s chikungunya outbreak escalates: On 4 March 2026 the Ministry of Health confirmed local transmission with over 1,357 laboratory-confirmed cases and one death; another pending. Chikungunya, an arbovirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; the virus is not transmitted directly from person to person, and causes fever, severe joint pain/swelling, headache, fatigue, and sometimes rash; infection confers lifelong immunity. The 2014 outbreak involved 700 tested cases; the current spread is faster. Rainy season (mid-April–August) may amplify transmission.

articleHeadline: Sharp rise in meningococcal disease cases reported in Việt Nam
articleSummary: Việt Nam reports a sharp rise in invasive meningococcal disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis, with 95 cases in the past year vs 21 the year before and 3 deaths. November 2025 saw 11 meningococcal meningitis cases, signaling ongoing winter-spring transmission. Five serogroups circulate—A, B, C, W, Y—with serogroup W linked to higher mortality. Transmission is via respiratory droplets and close contact; many teens and young adults are asymptomatic carriers. Without treatment, mortality can reach 50%; with treatment, 8–15%. About 20% of survivors have complications. Early antibiotics within 24 hours improve survival. Early symptoms resemble flu: fever, headache, fatigue, vomiting; meningitis signs include stiff neck; septic shock may present with a rash. Vaccination uses Menactra (A, C, W, Y) from nine months with age-based dosing; Bexsero (B) from two months. Vaccines are available at Việt Nam FMP clinics; vaccination is advised for infants, adolescents, dorm residents, and others at risk.
notes: 前年度21例から95例への急増（4.5倍）、死亡者3名、複数血清群（A, B, C, W, Y）の循環、血清群Wの高い致命率、冬春季の継続的な伝播が確認されている。十代から若年成人を含む広範な年齢層が影響を受け、不顕性感染者による継続的な伝播リスクがある。

articleHeadline: Invisible danger in traditional dishes alarms health authorities
articleSummary: Five severe botulinum toxin poisoning cases in Da Nang linked to fermented fish highlight ongoing risk in Vietnam. Clostridium botulinum produces botulinum toxin in anaerobic, sealed foods; exposure can cause muscle paralysis and respiratory failure, often fatal without prompt treatment. Vietnam has seen prior outbreaks: 2020 Quang Nam (home-fermented carp) with drooping eyelids and limb weakness; 2023 Ho Chi Minh City cluster after fermented fish and homemade paste requiring mechanical ventilation; 2024 Binh Duong case from fermented snakehead fish. High-risk foods include home-canned, fermented fish/meat, fish sauce, pate, and sealed products. BAT (Botulinum Antitoxin) is scarce and expensive (~US$8,000 per vial); Vietnam facilities often rely on WHO stockpiles in Geneva. Early administration within 48–72 hours can shorten ventilation and aid recovery; delays worsen outcomes. Prevention stressed: avoid damaged packaging, thoroughly boil/steam canned foods for at least 10 minutes and seek urgent care for symptoms such as ptosis, dysphagia, and weakness.
notes: 記事サマリーはベトナムのダナン、ホーチミン市、ビンズオン省での複数の重篤なボツリヌス毒素中毒事例に焦点を当てている。スイス/ジュネーブは抗毒素備蓄地としてのみ言及されており、実際の発生地はベトナムのみ。医療資源の深刻な不足（抗毒素1バイアルあたり8,000米ドル）と高い致死率の可能性が懸念される。WPRO基準全5項目が該当し、シグナルの確実性が高い。

articleHeadline: Hepatitis C drug may prevent hepatitis E virus replication
articleSummary: Global hepatitis E virus (HEV) fatalities are about 70,000 annually; currently no vaccine or specific therapy exists. An international team from Germany (Bochum and Heidelberg) and China (Beijing) reports that a nucleoside/nucleotide analogue compound named 'Bamnfosbuvir' (as transliterated) effectively suppresses HEV replication. The compound is already under clinical evaluation for hepatitis C, suggesting potential for rapid repurposing if subsequent studies confirm safety and efficacy. The findings, published March 6, 2026 in the medical journal Gut, mark a notable advancement and indicate cross-activity of HCV antivirals against HEV. If further research succeeds, the approach could save millions of lives worldwide by providing a much-needed therapeutic option in the absence of a HEV vaccine. The study emphasizes urgent demand for HEV prevention and treatment.

articleHeadline: Bộ Y tế đề xuất 9 bệnh truyền nhiễm phải cách ly y tế, thực hiện ngay sau vài giờ phát hiện
articleSummary: Nine infectious diseases are proposed for mandatory medical isolation in Vietnam: diphtheria, pertussis, measles, rubella, anthrax, meningococcal meningitis, hand, foot and mouth disease, varicella (chickenpox), and mumps. The draft also allows isolation for other Group B infections as determined by the Minister of Health. Isolation targets four groups: patients, suspected cases, carriers, and those exposed to the pathogen; four modes: home-based isolation (decided by the commune chair), hospital isolation (by hospital director), and border quarantine (by border agency head). The proposal enables requisition of facilities such as schools, dormitories, military/police facilities, hotels, factories, and housing blocks. Isolation durations align with ministerial guidance or WHO recommendations. Processing is tightly timed: within 3 hours of detection, the commune health authority drafts a home isolation list; within 1 hour, the commune chair issues the order; within 3 hours more, notification and implementation occur. A temporary hold up to 3 hours may be imposed on suspected cases; coercive isolation with police involvement is allowed. State budgets fund isolation activities. Amid Nipah virus concerns, nationwide surveillance and infection control are urged as of 23 March 2026.

articleSummary: Vietnam will integrate tuberculosis (TB) screening into annual periodic health examinations starting in 2026, shifting from curative to preventive care. In 2025, TB detection reached over 119,000 cases (about 63% of new infections), with more than 12,000 TB deaths annually. Currently, only about 63% of TB patients are detected; roughly 40% are asymptomatic and diagnosed late. Despite ongoing health checks, only ~23% of people are screened, while 40–50% of the population lack TB screening despite 52 million employed individuals having annual checkups. It calls for chest X-ray screening with GeneXpert testing if abnormalities are found, integration with respiratory care at primary facilities, and guaranteed funding for screening, detection, and treatment under the national program. Early detection enables free treatment and reduces transmission.

articleSummary: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) poses a silent threat in Vietnam, per Dr. Nguyen Thanh Huyen of the National Lung Hospital.
